matches.stipulation: EIGHT MAN LADDER MATCH -- the belt hangs above the ring; wrestlers can also be eliminated by pinfall or submission; all falls count anywhere (announced live by Mark McMahon in-ring)
matches.note: For the AICW World Championship (crowned for the first time this show). With Davis, Legion, Loki, and Martin X eliminated, the remaining four (Payne, Bane, Smith, Ice Cold) raced for the belt above the ring via ladder. Nicky De Niro (from the earlier International Title match) interfered by yanking the rope just as Johnny Payne reached for the belt, costing him the title. In the final sequence Kyle Bane and Johnny Smith both grabbed the belt simultaneously atop the ladder; Ice Cold knocked the ladder out from under them and both men fell still holding the belt, with Bane coming up holding it and declared the winner. Payne, Smith, and Ice Cold were not formally announced as "eliminated" -- the match simply ended when Bane secured the belt.

date.source: No dateline survives in the document itself. Bracketed by the title lineage: its own main event bills "Hard Line" Byron Brady as the reigning AICW World Heavyweight Champion challenged by former champion Kyle Bane -- a reign that began at New Year's Revolution (25 January 1998) -- while the Tokyo Thunder Festival (29 March-1 April 1998) opens with Kyle Bane already the reigning champion again, and its own AICW Television Championship holder, "Pretty Boy" Troy Walcott, is billed there as defending a reign of "over two months," consistent with his own New Year's Revolution win. Both facts place this show between the two, in February or March 1998.
